newsitem.title: CHINA: China business climate to rebound in Q4 - survey.
newsitem.headline: China business climate to rebound in Q4 - survey.

text.p: China's business climate deteriorated in the third quarter of 1996, but was expected to rebound in the last quarter, state media said on Thursday, quoting a survey by the State Statistical Bureau.

The year-on-year profit growth of Chinese enterprises, especially those in the manufacturing sector, slipped in the third quarter compared with the second quarter, the China Daily said. It did not elaborate.

But 81.2 percent of 10,000 business people interviewed believed the business climate would not deteriorate further or would improve in the fourth quarter, Hong Kong's Beijing-backed Wen Wei Po newspaper said.
Only 17.4 percent of the respondents forecast the business climate worsening, Wen Wei Po said.
"Enterprises generally were confident about the October-December season," the Xinhua news agency said, quoting the survey.

The quarterly survey showed that only 33 percent of the respondents complained that interest rates were high compared with 67 percent in the second quarter, Xinhua said. The government has lowered interest rates twice this year.
The downturn in the third quarter was attributed in part to severe floods, Xinhua said.
The China Daily said 65.5 percent of Chinese enterprises attributed their difficulties to a shortage of working capital.

Many enterprises said the dearth of working capital was preventing them from making necessary technical renovations, the China Daily said, adding that financially troubled firms became even more vulnerable to market competition.
Some blamed mounting debts incurred by businesses themselves, while others attributed the downturn to strong domestic competition or flagging sales, the newspaper said.
The value-added output of China's industries reached 1357.5 billion yuan ($163.6 billion) in the first nine months, up 12.9 percent from the year-ago period, the China Daily said.
State-owned factories were affected most by the government's tight credit policy, the newspaper said. Their production growth stood at 5.5 percent from January to September.
Experts from the State Statistical Bureau said it was important to push ahead with reform of industrial enterprises to force them to be more competitive.
They also urged the central bank to make structural adjustments in loan provision in favour of companies in difficulties, while sticking to its tight monetary policy.
